chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Fadalah ibn Ayyub, from Ibn Bukayr, from Ubayd ibn Zur'arah, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who takes vinegar and turns it into vinegar [or: takes wine and turns it into vinegar], he said, 'There is no harm [in it].'

key_terms.لاَ بَأْسَ: There is no harm / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is vinegar derived from wine permissible in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the principle of *tabdil* (transformation), where wine (*khamr*) becomes vinegar (*khal*) through natural fermentation, thereby removing its impurity (*najis*) and making it permissible to consume. It highlights the Shia juristic view that the substance's identity changes fundamentally, distinguishing it from the original intoxicant, a key concept in deriving rulings on food and drink purity.
